title: A large public project can enter formal review with the preferred solution already narrowing the choices
source_unit: GAO-26-108193 review of Department of Energy Office of Environmental Management mission-need statements and planning for large capital projects
geography: United States Department of Energy environmental-management sites; large projects estimated at $100 million or more

observations.period: 2026 GAO review of large-project planning; mission-need statements and selected project discussions

denominator.unit: DOE Environmental Management mission-need statements for large projects estimated at least $100 million

predetermined_solution.value: the majority of reviewed mission-need statements identified a particular solution even though DOE standards say the statement should identify a need without selecting the solution

option_exclusion.value: GAO found instances where potential cost-saving options were not considered or pursued after a preferred solution was identified early

technical_alternative.value: experts described a technically sound, cheaper treatment that was not pursued because of an existing regulatory agreement, followed by years of spending on a solution later deemed suboptimal and suspended

independent_review.value: existing mission-need reviews did not include independent experts; DOE concurred with recommendations to add them

project_value_and_outcome.value: not observed as a common cost, schedule, safety, cleanup, or community outcome series
project_value_and_outcome.unit: missing project-level option set, cost comparison, delivery, risk, and public-impact ledger

observations.method: GAO analyzed 21 DOE Environmental Management mission-need statements, qualitative material from three expert discussion groups involving 12 experts, and interviews with headquarters and field staff at sites with large projects.
observations.uncertainty: The review identifies planning and oversight conditions rather than estimating the causal cost of every predetermined solution. Expert discussion groups and selected project examples are not a representative outcome sample, and legal, regulatory, technical, and site constraints may limit the feasible option set.
observations.subgroup: DOE Environmental Management large capital projects, mission-need reviewers, contractors, regulators, independent experts, national laboratories, and affected sites; project scale and waste type differ.
observations.counterinterpretation: Naming a solution early may reflect genuine technical, legal, safety, or regulatory constraints, and later planning may still consider alternatives. An independent review may widen options without guaranteeing a cheaper, faster, safer, or more acceptable project.

boundary: This record measures early option framing and review design in selected DOE cleanup projects. It does not establish waste-treatment failure, contractor wrongdoing, national cleanup performance, taxpayer loss, environmental harm, or the outcome of DOE's later recommendations.
